gaps: The owner must be configured by stable Google account ID, but the spec gives the deployer no way to obtain or verify that ID; the Accounts profile exposes the Google email instead. Owner access cannot be reliably provisioned from the documented flow (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:25; docs/specs/accounts.md:99).

The creator becomes a circle's first member, but join events are specified for joining through an invite. The spec does not say whether circle creation records a join, so two implementations can produce different join counts (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:42; docs/specs/circles.md:25; docs/specs/circles.md:68).

Search events must carry the chosen bank and type, but the confirmed Find and contact contract lists only the searcher, circles and number found. The event producer and its acceptance criterion do not require these fields, leaving the Searched cards table without a binding input contract (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:45; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:48; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:115).

The privacy notice describes usage events linked to the acting member and circle, but this spec also links WhatsApp taps to the card holder and stores search bank and type. It does not require those additional data uses to be disclosed or address Accounts' rule for accepting a changed notice (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:45; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:46; docs/specs/accounts.md:67; docs/specs/accounts.md:81).

The spec says every event except a failed WhatsApp tap is always recorded, but does not define what happens when recording fails for a join, card addition, search, or Copy/Share tap. In particular, whether the user action is refused, rolled back, or allowed without a count remains unsettled (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:49; docs/specs/circles.md:41; docs/specs/cards.md:67).

The view must count circles created by someone other than the owner, including deleted circles, but the retained circle data specified here omits whether the owner created each circle. The spec also leaves historical classification undefined if the configured owner changes (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:29; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:57; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:70).

After deletion removes a person's identifiers from events, the spec does not say whether historical distinct active-member and contacted-card-holder counts drop, remain fixed through nonidentifying aggregates, or use another rule. Only raw event counts and new-member counts have explicit deletion behavior (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:51; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:67; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:69; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:131).

The per-circle table requires a separate row for every circle but specifies only its name and deleted label for identification. Circle names need not be unique, so two current circles, or two deleted circles with the same last name, can produce indistinguishable rows (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:75; docs/specs/circles.md:23).
contradictions: This spec retains timestamped individual events with circle and search attributes after removing a deleted member's identifier, while the confirmed Accounts contract says their events remain only as anonymous counts. Both retention shapes cannot be implemented as written (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:48; docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:53; docs/specs/accounts.md:120).

The Searched cards table says its bank-and-type found-nobody count shows which cards members' circles lack. A variant-filtered search can find nobody even when members hold that bank and type, so the stated interpretation is false (docs/specs/usage-metrics.md:86; docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:32).
resolutions: Each member's own profile shows their Google account ID to them alone, so the owner can copy it into configuration.
Creating a circle records no join event; it counts as a new circle.
The spec explicitly extends the Find and contact search event with bank and type (roadmap CWF-4 carries it).
The first privacy-notice version discloses the card-holder link on taps and the bank and type on searches, so no re-acceptance is triggered.
One rule for all five events: recording never blocks, delays or undoes the action; a failed record goes uncounted.
Every circle records at creation whether the configured owner created it; later owner changes do not reclassify; the flag survives deletion.
Distinct active-member and card-holder counts drop when a member deletes their account.
Per-circle rows show name and creation date so same-named circles are distinguishable.
Retained events keep time, circles and search bank and type with no member identifier and are used only for counts, which is how Accounts' anonymous-counts rule is met.
Searched cards description now says how often searches, including variant filters, found nobody, not which cards circles lack.

artifact_delta.final:
- Every member's own profile shows their Google account ID to them alone, so
  the owner can copy theirs into the configuration. It is never shown to
  another member (Accounts).

artifact_delta.cold:
- A WhatsApp tap whose recording fails goes uncounted, as Find and contact
  requires; every other event is always recorded.
artifact_delta.final:
- This spec extends the search event defined by Find and contact with the
  chosen bank and type; the app records them with every search.
- Creating a circle does not record a join event; it is counted as a new
  circle instead.
- Recording an event never blocks, delays or undoes the member's action. If
  recording fails, that event goes uncounted; this applies to all five events,
  as Find and contact already requires for WhatsApp taps.
- The privacy notice's description of usage events (Accounts) includes that a
  WhatsApp tap records the card holder contacted and that a search records the
  bank and type searched. This is part of the first notice version, so it
  triggers no re-acceptance.

they appear in; the events stay with their time, circles and search bank and
  type but no member identifier, and are used only to produce counts. This is
  how the Accounts rule that events "remain only as anonymous counts" is met.

artifact_delta.cold:
- When a circle is deleted, its events stay, and its last name, creation time
  and deletion are kept so the view can show and count it (Circles).
artifact_delta.final:
- Distinct active-member and card-holder counts only count identities still on
  events, so they drop when a member deletes their account.
- Every circle records, when it is created, whether its creator was the
  configured owner at that moment; a later change of owner does not reclassify
  existing circles.
- When a circle is deleted, its events stay, and its last name, creation time,
  deletion and owner-created flag are kept so the view can show and count it
  (Circles).
